buckets.title: Surface Areas and Volumes
buckets.badge_reason: Formulas are frequently misapplied by confusing open vs closed boundaries and composite solid hidden interfaces.

capabilities.action: Calculate surface area and volume of cubes and cuboids with metric unit conversion.
capabilities.success_criterion: Apply TSA = 6 a² for cubes and V = l × w × h for cuboids, converting units (1 m³ = 1000 L).

capabilities.action: Compute curved and total surface area of cylinders, distinguishing diameter from radius.
capabilities.success_criterion: Convert diameter to radius (r = d/2) before applying CSA = 2πrh.

capabilities.action: Formulate boundary surface models for open and hollow vessels.
capabilities.success_criterion: Include only physical boundary faces (e.g. 2πrh + πr² for open bucket), excluding openings and unpainted faces.

capabilities.action: Derive cone slant height using Pythagoras and compute conical surface area.
capabilities.success_criterion: Apply l = √(r² + h²) to find slant height and calculate curved area πrl.

capabilities.action: Calculate surface area and volume of spheres and hemispheres, distinguishing open from solid.
capabilities.success_criterion: Select 2πr² for open hollow hemisphere inner surface vs 3πr² for solid hemisphere.

capabilities.action: Determine exposed boundary surface area of composite solids.
capabilities.success_criterion: Sum only exposed curved faces, excluding internal hidden contact interfaces.

capabilities.action: Apply conservation of volume during recasting and explain non-conservation of surface area.

microtopics.title: Cubes and Cuboids: Surface Area and Volume Measures
microtopics.badge_reason: Direct formula evaluation with unit conversions between m³ and litres.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Identify whether total surface area (6 faces) or internal capacity (volume) is requested, and convert volume units (1 m³ = 1000 litres).

teaching_path.action: Identify 3D solid type and required measure (surface area vs capacity).
teaching_path.why_valid: Boundary area requires face summation; capacity requires volume.

teaching_path.action: Apply TSA = 6a² or V = l × b × h, converting units to litres where required.
teaching_path.why_valid: Capacity in litres is volume in m³ multiplied by 1000.

teaching_path.action: Verify dimensional consistency: area is length², volume is length³.
teaching_path.why_valid: Physical units verify algebraic scaling.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Confusing volume (a³) with total surface area (6a²).
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If edge is 7 cm, is 343 the surface area or the volume?
misconceptions.repair: Volume is 7³ = 343 cm³; total surface area is 6 × 7² = 294 cm².

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Cubes and Cuboids: Surface Area and Volume Measures; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: Find the total surface area of a cube of edge 5 cm, and state its volume in cm³.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Checks simultaneous calculation of surface area and volume for a regular cube.

construction_units.decision: Identify whether total surface area (6 faces) or internal capacity (volume) is requested, and convert volume units (1 m³ = 1000 litres).

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

microtopics.title: Cylinders: Diameter Trap and Curved Surface Area
microtopics.badge_reason: Commonly fails when students substitute diameter directly instead of radius.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Halve diameter to find radius r = d/2 before evaluating curved surface area 2πrh.

teaching_path.action: Extract diameter from problem statement and halve it to obtain base radius r = d/2.
teaching_path.why_valid: Curved surface area formula 2πrh strictly requires radius, not diameter.

teaching_path.action: Substitute radius r and height h into CSA = 2πrh.
teaching_path.why_valid: Formula represents circumference (2πr) swept along height h.

teaching_path.action: Check result using alternate form CSA = πdh directly.
teaching_path.why_valid: πdh avoids division and multiplication by 2, verifying the calculation.

misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If diameter is 14 cm, what value should be plugged into 2πrh for r?
misconceptions.repair: Radius is half diameter: r = 14 / 2 = 7 cm. Using 14 doubles the actual area.

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Cylinders: Diameter Trap and Curved Surface Area; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: A cylinder has diameter 28 cm and height 10 cm. Find its curved surface area using π = 22/7.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Evaluates diameter conversion and curved surface area computation.

construction_units.decision: Halve diameter to find radius r = d/2 before evaluating curved surface area 2πrh.

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

microtopics.title: Open Cylindrical Containers: Exposed Boundary Selection
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires excluding the open top face from total surface area calculations.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Recognize that an open cylinder consists of the curved wall (2πrh) and one base (πr²), never two bases.

teaching_path.action: Inspect physical container boundary and identify which faces require material.
teaching_path.why_valid: Only exposed boundaries separate the interior from the outside; open faces require no sheet.

teaching_path.action: Build a surface inventory: curved wall, bottom face, and top opening. Mark only material faces as countable.
teaching_path.why_valid: An opening is not a material surface; inventorying boundaries before formulas prevents adding a non-existent lid.
teaching_path.output: A countable-surface inventory with no numerical result

teaching_path.action: Verify that total area is strictly less than closed cylinder TSA by πr².
teaching_path.why_valid: Subtracting top circular face confirms consistency with standard closed solid.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Using closed cylinder TSA formula 2πr(h + r) for an open container.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does an open cylindrical bucket have a metal lid on top?
misconceptions.repair: No, an open bucket has no top cover. Add only 1 circular base: 2πrh + πr².

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Open Cylindrical Containers: Exposed Boundary Selection; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: An open cylindrical can has radius 3.5 cm and height 10 cm. Find the area of tin sheet required to make it (use π = 22/7).

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Verifies boundary area calculation for an open cylinder.

answer.check: Closed cylinder would be 220 + 77 = 297 cm²; 297 - 38.5 = 258.5 cm² confirms open boundary.

construction_units.decision: Inventory which boundaries are material surfaces and which are openings before forming any area expression.

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

microtopics.title: Cones: Slant Height Derivation and Curved Surface Area
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires calculating slant height via Pythagoras before evaluating curved surface area.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Derive slant height l = √(r² + h²) from the vertical right triangle before calculating curved surface area πrl.

teaching_path.action: Identify radius r and vertical height h from problem statement.
teaching_path.why_valid: Vertical axis, radius, and slant generator form a right-angled triangle.

teaching_path.action: Compute slant height l = √(r² + h²), then evaluate CSA = πrl.
teaching_path.why_valid: Curved surface area formula requires generator slant length l, not vertical height h.

teaching_path.action: Confirm slant height l > h and l > r; verify canvas area exceeds horizontal footprint πr².
teaching_path.why_valid: Hypotenuse must exceed legs; sloping canopy area must exceed flat base.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Using vertical height h directly in place of slant height l in πrl.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: In a conical tent, is the sloping canvas along the vertical pole or along the slanted side?
misconceptions.repair: Canvas lies along the sloping generator of length l = √(r² + h²). Using vertical height h underestimates the required canvas.

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Cones: Slant Height Derivation and Curved Surface Area; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: Find the curved surface area of a cone of base radius 6 m and vertical height 8 m (take π = 3.14).

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Verifies Pythagorean slant height derivation and cone curved surface evaluation.

answer.check: Base area is 3.14 × 36 = 113.04 m²; CSA = 188.4 > 113.04 as required for a sloped surface.

construction_units.decision: Derive slant height l = √(r² + h²) from the vertical right triangle before calculating curved surface area πrl.

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

microtopics.title: Hemispheres: Curved Inner Surface versus Circular Opening
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires selecting hemisphere volume formula (2/3)πr³ and cubing the radius.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Evaluate hemisphere internal capacity using V = (2/3)πr³, ensuring r is cubed and volume is halved relative to full sphere.

teaching_path.action: Identify the bowl's material inner boundary and distinguish it from the circular mouth.
teaching_path.why_valid: The circular mouth is an opening; the inner material is the curved half-sphere surface.
teaching_path.output: Curved material surface identified; mouth excluded

teaching_path.action: Relate the curved area of a hemisphere to half of a sphere's surface area.
teaching_path.why_valid: A sphere has surface area 4πr², so the curved half-sphere boundary is half of that area; no flat circular face is added for an open bowl.
teaching_path.output: A curved-surface relation, with the opening still excluded

teaching_path.action: Check the model by asking whether any physical flat disk exists across the mouth of the bowl.
teaching_path.why_valid: If there is no material disk, total-solid-hemisphere area is the wrong model.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Using full sphere volume formula (4/3)πr³ or surface area formula 2πr² for capacity.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: How much liquid does a hemisphere hold compared to a full sphere of the same radius?
misconceptions.repair: A hemisphere holds exactly half of a full sphere: (1/2) × (4/3)πr³ = (2/3)πr³.

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Spheres and Hemispheres: Capacity and Volume; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: Find the capacity of a hemispherical bowl of radius 7 cm in cm³ (use π = 22/7).

construction_units.decision: Treat the bowl's circular mouth as an opening and build the inner-area model only from the curved hemispherical material surface.

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

grade9v3:interactive_idea.learner_manipulates: An assembly/separation slider that moves a cone toward and away from a hemisphere sharing radius r, with independent sliders for base radius r and cone height h.
grade9v3:interactive_idea.becomes_visible: When separated (gap > 0), the two circular base faces are highlighted in amber as exposed surface area (TSA = Cone TSA + Hemisphere TSA); when joined (gap = 0), the contact faces turn dashed/gray and are struck out from the live area ledger, leaving only the curved surfaces (Exposed Area = πrl + 2πr²); dragging r and h recalculates the slant height triangle and live numerical values.
grade9v3:interactive_idea.misconception_targeted: Adding the total surface area of the cone to the total surface area of the hemisphere, erroneously counting the internal joint face twice.

microtopics.title: Composite Solids: Hidden Boundary Exclusion
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires excluding joined interior interfaces and summing only exposed boundary surfaces.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Identify the exposed boundary faces of joined solids (CSA cone + CSA hemisphere), strictly excluding the joined circular interface.

teaching_path.action: Inspect composite solid and identify where component solids join.
teaching_path.why_valid: When solids are glued together, their touching faces become internal and cannot be touched.

teaching_path.action: Label every contact face INTERNAL and every reachable outer face EXPOSED before selecting any surface-area formulas.
teaching_path.why_valid: A joined interface lies inside the composite object and cannot contribute to exposed boundary area.

teaching_path.action: Check the inventory by imagining painting the outside without separating the joined solids.
teaching_path.why_valid: A paint test catches hidden faces that were accidentally counted as exposed.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Adding the total surface area of the cone to the total surface area of the hemisphere.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Can you paint the circular base where the cone meets the hemisphere in the toy?
misconceptions.repair: No, that circular face is inside the toy. Only external surfaces are painted: CSA(cone) + CSA(hemisphere).

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Composite Solids: Hidden Boundary Exclusion; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: A solid toy is formed by a cone of radius 3 cm and slant height 5 cm mounted on a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. Find its total surface area in terms of π.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Verifies boundary exclusion in composite solid surface area.

reasoning: Exposed conical surface = πrl = π × 3 × 5 = 15π cm².
answer.check: Closed cone TSA = 15π + 9π = 24π; closed hemisphere TSA = 18π + 9π = 27π; sum = 51π. Subtracting 2 joined faces: 51π - 18π = 33π cm².

construction_units.decision: Distinguish exposed outer surfaces from the internal joining interface before constructing the question-specific area sum.

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

microtopics.title: Recasting Solids: Volume Invariance and Surface Area Expansion
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires recognizing that volume is conserved under recasting while surface area increases upon subdivision.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Equate initial material volume to total recast volume (V_initial = n * V_final) and recognize that dividing matter increases surface area.

teaching_path.action: State conservation of material volume under melting and casting without loss.
teaching_path.why_valid: Mass and extensive volume are invariant during phase change.

teaching_path.action: Equate volumes V_initial = n × V_final to solve for count n = (R/r)³.
teaching_path.why_valid: Ratio of total volume to single unit volume gives the integer count of recast solids.

teaching_path.action: Compute total surface area of all n recast objects and compare with original surface area.
teaching_path.why_valid: Dividing a solid exposes internal material as new external boundaries, increasing surface area by factor R/r.
teaching_path.output: Verified count and surface area scaling

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Assuming that total surface area is conserved when a solid is melted into smaller pieces.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: If you cut an apple into 8 slices, do the slices have more skin/cut area to paint than the whole apple?
misconceptions.repair: Cutting or recasting exposes internal material as new surface area. Volume is conserved, but surface area increases by the linear scaling ratio R/r.

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Recasting Solids: Volume Invariance and Surface Area Expansion; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: A solid metal sphere of radius 4 cm is melted and recast into small spheres of radius 2 cm. Find the number of small spheres and the ratio of total final surface area to initial surface area.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Verifies volume conservation and surface area expansion under recasting.

answer.summary: 8 small spheres; total surface area doubles (ratio 2:1).
answer.check: 8 × (4/3)π(2³) = 8 × (32/3)π = 256/3 π cm³ = (4/3)π(4³) confirms exact volume conservation.

construction_units.decision: Equate initial material volume to total recast volume (V_initial = n * V_final) and recognize that dividing matter increases surface area.

independent_checks.statement: Check units (cm² or m²) and physical dimensional consistency.
Substitute computed parameters back into governing relation to confirm arithmetic identity.
Confirm physical boundary conditions and domain constraints.

microtopics.title: Dimensional Invariants: Cone and Cylinder Volume Ratio
microtopics.badge_reason: Requires applying the 1:3 ratio between cone and cylinder of equal base and height.
entry_assumptions: Can calculate 2D areas of rectangles (l × w) and circles (πr²).
Can evaluate algebraic formulas using rational numbers with π = 22/7.
microtopics.inferential_jump: Apply the geometric invariant that a cone occupies exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with identical base radius and height.

teaching_path.action: Identify equal geometric parameters (identical base radius r and vertical height h).
teaching_path.why_valid: The two solids share base area A = πr² and height h.

teaching_path.action: Express cone volume (1/3)πr²h as (1/3) of cylinder volume πr²h.
teaching_path.why_valid: Volume of a pyramid/cone is 1/3 the volume of a prism/cylinder of equal base and altitude.

teaching_path.action: Verify by multiplying by 3: 3 × V_cone = V_cylinder.
teaching_path.why_valid: Inverse multiplication confirms the rational proportional relation.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Believing a cone has half the volume of a cylinder of equal base and height.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Does it take 2 or 3 conical water cups to fill a cylindrical glass of the same radius and height?
misconceptions.repair: It takes exactly 3 conical cups. The factor is 1/3, not 1/2.

microtopics.research_contribution: Author-created structured pedagogical framing for Dimensional Invariants: Cone and Cylinder Volume Ratio; independent review pending.

exit_task.prompt: A cone and a cylinder have equal base radius and equal height. If the cylinder volume is 90 cm³, find the volume of the cone.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: Verifies 1:3 proportional volume invariant between cone and cylinder.

construction_units.decision: Apply the geometric invariant that a cone occupies exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with identical base radius and height.

relations.meaning: The total surface area of a cube is the sum of its 6 congruent square faces, and volume is the cube of the edge length.

derivation.action: Calculate area of one square face: A = a * a = a².
Multiply by 6 disjoint congruent faces: TSA = 6 * a².
derivation.why_valid: Additivity of surface areas of non-overlapping faces.

relations.meaning: Curved surface area equals base circumference times height; total surface area includes both circular end caps.

derivation.action: Unroll lateral curved face into a rectangle with width 2πr and height h.
derivation.why_valid: Boundary unrolling preserves metric distance along generators.

relations.meaning: Surface area of a cylindrical container open at the top consists of the curved wall and exactly one circular bottom base.
conditions: Container is open at top; thickness is negligible.

derivation.action: Identify exposed boundary components: curved wall (2πrh) and one base (πr²).
derivation.why_valid: Top is open, so its area is excluded from the boundary.

checks: A_open is strictly less than closed cylinder TSA = 2πrh + 2πr² by exactly πr².

relations.meaning: Slant height is the hypotenuse of the vertical right triangle; curved surface area equals π times base radius times slant height.

derivation.action: Apply Pythagoras' theorem: l² = r² + h².
derivation.why_valid: Radius and vertical axis are perpendicular in a right circular cone.

limits: l must be strictly greater than both r and h.
checks: If h = 0, l = r and CSA = πr² (flat disk limit).

relations.meaning: A hemisphere holds half the volume of a sphere of identical radius.

derivation.why_valid: A hemisphere is exactly half a sphere by plane reflection symmetry.

checks: Volume of 2 identical hemispheres equals 1 sphere.

relations.meaning: Exposed boundary area of a cone mounted on a hemisphere consists of the cone curved face plus the hemisphere curved face, excluding the internal circular joint.

symbols.meaning: Common radius of cone and hemisphere

conditions: Cone and hemisphere share identical base radius.
Joint circular face is inside the solid.

derivation.why_valid: Total exposed surface area is the sum of disjoint exterior boundary faces.

limits: Circular interface is inside the solid and must not be counted.
checks: TSA is strictly less than TSA(cone) + TSA(hemisphere) by exactly 2πr².

relations.meaning: Material volume is conserved under recasting without loss; the number of small similar objects scales as the cube of the linear dimension ratio.
conditions: No material is lost during melting or casting.

derivation.why_valid: Conservation of mass and extensive volume.

checks: Total volume of n small spheres equals original sphere volume.

relations.meaning: A cone occupies exactly one-third the volume of a cylinder with the same base radius and vertical height.
conditions: Equal base radius r and equal vertical height h.

derivation.why_valid: Volume formula for pyramids and cones relative to prisms and cylinders.

limits: Applies only when base and altitude are strictly identical.
